title: StockSelectionRequestV1
description: A stock selection in one of two modes. `criteria` is a query over a region's universe: filters are ANDed, `sort` orders the matches and `limit` caps the page at 20 rows. `symbols` is an explicit ticker list resolved inside the universe addressed by `snapshot_id`. The response carries `total` (every row that matched) separately from `returned` (the page), so a 20-row display never claims to be a 20-stock market.

mode.description: Which question is being asked; the two modes share no knobs.

region.description: Criteria only: the universe tab to query.

asset_class.description: Both modes: the instrument family. `stock` (default) and `etf` are different universes — `us_etf` implies `etf`, and `global` is stock-only. The ETF universe is `type=fund` + `subtype=etf` with no market-cap floor and the same OTC exclusion.

view.description: Both modes: shape every response row as one of the six Finviz views. A viewed row carries `rank`/`symbol`/`as_of` plus one cell per declared view column, filled from the parity metrics the bulk scan carries (missing columns stay null, never 0); without `view` the row is the light screen row.

filters.description: ANDed predicates; an empty list is the identity. A key with no light row column is refused with a 422 naming the missing metric — never ignored, because an ignored filter returns the unfiltered screen.

sort.description: The one visible metric the page is ordered by.

limit.description: Page size. Clamped to 20: a larger value is not an error, it simply cannot widen the display, and the response reports the limit that was applied.

symbols.description: Symbols only: tickers in the order the response should list them. A ticker the universe does not carry is reported in `missing`.

source.description: Symbols only: the provenance the snapshot must declare. A source the snapshot was not built from is refused, never relabelled.

snapshot_id.description: Symbols only: the snapshot whose region and rule version the tickers are resolved against. It fixes *which* universe, not the prices — the rows are read fresh and dated by the response's `as_of`, never by the snapshot's.

filter.description: One predicate: exactly one of `key` (a Finviz filter key, resolved to its row column) or `field` (the column itself), plus an operator and a value.

key.description: One of the 82 Finviz filter keys. The 7 that filter a light row today, and the 75 that are refused with their reason, are listed in x-filter-keys.

value.description: The comparison value. `in` and `between` take an array (`between` exactly two numbers); every other operator takes one scalar. Finviz option tokens (`mega`, `u5`, `ob70`) are display buckets, not values: send the number the bucket means.

idx.label: Index
idx.reason: needs index membership (S&P 500, Nasdaq-100, Dow, Russell): the scan has no index-constituent column, and a market-cap threshold is not a membership test

industry.label: Industry
industry.reason: needs an industry classification: the row carries `sector` only, and the scanner's industry vocabulary has not been probed

fa_div.label: Dividend Yield
fa_div.reason: needs dividend metrics (yield, growth, payout ratio): the scan carries no dividend column

sh_short.label: Short Float
sh_short.reason: needs a short-interest column the scanner fills: `short_float` answered null for all 5,720 US rows (and 96,278 global rows) when probed live, so a filter on it can only return an empty screen

an_recom.label: Analyst Recom.
an_recom.reason: needs Finviz's 1-5 analyst score: the scanner's `Recommend.All` is a -1..+1 mean rating, so a filter written on Finviz's scale (2 = buy) matches nothing — the column is carried for display, not for this key

sh_opt.label: Option/Short
sh_opt.reason: needs an optionable/shortable flag: the scan carries no such column

sh_trades.label: Trades
sh_trades.reason: needs a trade-count column: the scan carries no trades counter

ipodate.label: IPO Date
ipodate.reason: needs an IPO-date column the scanner fills: `ipo_date` answered null for all 5,720 US rows (and 96,278 global rows) when probed live, so a filter on it can only return an empty screen

theme.label: Theme
theme.reason: needs theme/sub-theme classification: the scan carries no theme column

subtheme.reason: needs theme/sub-theme classification: the scan carries no theme column

fa_evsales.label: EV/Sales
fa_evsales.reason: needs enterprise value and sales as separate columns: only EV/EBITDA is copied, so EV/Sales cannot be formed

ta_perf.label: Performance
ta_perf.reason: spans ten performance windows (day, week, month, quarter, half-year, YTD, year, 3Y, 5Y, 10Y), while the row carries one column per window (`ret_1w` … `ret_10y`); a single key is not a single field — send the column instead

ta_perf2.label: Performance 2
ta_perf2.reason: spans ten performance windows (day, week, month, quarter, half-year, YTD, year, 3Y, 5Y, 10Y), while the row carries one column per window (`ret_1w` … `ret_10y`); a single key is not a single field — send the column instead

ta_volatility.label: Volatility
ta_volatility.reason: spans two windows (weekly and monthly), while the row carries `volatility_w` and `volatility_m` separately — send the column instead

ta_gap.label: Gap
ta_gap.reason: needs a gap column: the scan carries no open price, so the gap cannot be computed

ta_changeopen.label: Change from Open

ta_highlow20d.label: 20-Day High/Low
ta_highlow20d.reason: needs 20-day and 50-day high/low columns: the scan carries the 52-week extremes only

ta_highlow50d.label: 50-Day High/Low
ta_highlow50d.reason: needs 20-day and 50-day high/low columns: the scan carries the 52-week extremes only

ta_highlow52w.label: 52-Week High/Low
ta_highlow52w.reason: is a percent distance from the 52-week high/low, while the row carries the absolute `high_52w`/`low_52w` prices; the two units are not interchangeable — filter `high_52w`/`low_52w` directly

ta_alltime.label: All-Time High/Low
